               <ns0:p n="16">16 For men verily swear by the greater <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For</ns0:hi> here is only Narrative, introducing the amplifica<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Argument drawn from God's Promise and Oath, for the quickning those and all Believers to make ou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> after the full assurance of Hope, the Promise and Oath of God concerning them as well as <ns0:hi>Abraham.</ns0:hi> That since Mens Oaths procure Credit, and put an end to Doubts, Strife and Contradiction amongst them; much more should God's Oath put an end to doubts and gainsayings of Creatures, and make them to give Faith to him: Men are not In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venters and Authors of this Ordinance of Swearing, but subject to God's Precept requiring this from them, and in this special part of God's Worship instituted by him, they ought to swear justly and according to his Will; and swear they must by God only, who knows the intentions and se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crets of the Heart, and who is absolutely greater than all; the Omniscient, Omnipresent, Omnipotent and Sove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />reign Lord of all Persons, who knows false Swearers, and inflicts on them not only Temporal but Eternal Punishments. The Swearing by any other, God rebukes, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.13. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 4.2.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 22.11.</ns0:note> an oath for confirmation <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> to them an end of all strife <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">And in this special part of God's Worship, God is called in as a Co-Witness of the Truth of what is sworn, and as a Judg and Avenger of it, if it be otherwise; and so the Oath becomes a confirmation of Faith and Confidence of Men one in another, and of Love accompanying the same; so that if Strife, Doubt, Suspicion or Jealousy arise among them about either Words or Deeds, which are not known to those who doubt, and cannot be cleared by Sense or Reason, or any other way but a Testimony of some person who knows them, whose being insufficient of it self, calls in God by an Oath as Co-witness, with whom it is supposed he would not break his Interest, nor invocate him against himself, by declaring what is false: On this all Strife and Contradiction is to be decided among Men, and to cease, and so the Controversy to be determined.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">But it is the Heart only of a per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />severing Believer, not of common Professors, which is so strongly setled and comforted by them; such <ns0:hi>who fly to take hold of them,</ns0:hi> having cleared their Right to them, and possessing their Souls of them by Faith, so to hold fast, as who would no more leave, than <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> would the Horns of the Altar, being a far greater Security than it, or any City of Refuge whatso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ever; retreating to, and keeping in this Strong-hold, nothing can interrupt their Comfort, or hurt them, <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 13.15, 16. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 18, 10. <ns0:hi>The Hope set before them</ns0:hi> is that eternal good and blessed State which is reserved in Heaven for Believers, the Object of their Hope set out to their View and Prosecution as a Prize in the Promise, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.3, 4. by a Metonymy of the Effect for the Cause, are <ns0:hi>Hope,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Good hoped for,</ns0:hi> joyned together for our Pursuit.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Which <ns0:hi>hope</ns0:hi> we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Which,</ns0:hi> taketh in both the Good hoped for, and the Grace and Act it self of Hope exercised about it; which Grace is by a Metaphor set out to be to the Soul, what an <ns0:hi>Anchor</ns0:hi> is to Ships in a Tempest, when tossed with Gusts, and Storms, and Billows of Thoughts rouling one upon another to the over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />setting of it; this Hope staieth, strengthens, setleth it, even the Hope and Certainty of eternal Rest and Happiness secu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red to them by the Promise and Oath of God. This Hope is safe and firm efficiently, and makes the Soul in the midst of all the threatning Temptations from a tempestuous World, <ns0:hi>safe</ns0:hi>; because fastned on God's Promise; and <ns0:hi>firm,</ns0:hi> because strengthned by God's Oath, which will hold out all Tempests.</ns0:note>, and which en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />treth into that within the veil <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Hope,</ns0:hi> like an <ns0:hi>Anchor,</ns0:hi> is firmly placed, hath wrought it self into the best Holdfast, even the innermost part of the Veil. <ns0:hi>The Veil</ns0:hi> was that in the Tabernacle and Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, which separated the holy Place from the Holy of Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liest. Here it is that the Anchor of the Christians Hope is fastned; this sure Harbour, where no Tempest can reach or loosen it, but into which their Souls, after all their tossings in the tempestuous Ocean of this World, by the Hurricanes of Temptations, which made them quiver again, shall be over, will enter with a full Gale, and injoy that Rest and Blessedness for ever, which they had by God's Promise and Oath on which they relied, secured to them. See <ns0:hi>Colos.</ns0:hi> 1.5. and 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.3, 4, to 10.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
